title: Family bands with her brothers and later with her sons
summary: After Manetta retired to teach she played with her brothers Irving and Lawrence, then formed a trio and later quartet with her sons, now at Preservation Hall.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: He doesn't teach you. I think it's in the 20s. That's right. It's the early 20s, I think.
Then I started out with my brothers, Oivin and Longin. And Lawrence threw it. Oivin was a great trombonist. Lawrence was a trumpet, very good trumpet player and music arranger.
So you've always been in family bands most of the time. That's right. Still have you.

And I played for years with them until Oivin died. And Lawrence became very ill. Then I had to look for another way. Then this one here, that's my oldest boy. He was just fresh in from the Army. And Gerald was then 16 and Placif was 14. That's the two boys you've seen at the preservation hall. Well, we started out a trio there. And we've been together. Well, I said a trio. We first started the trio because Placif was in the Army. And when he came back, it was four pieces. And then we went along there.
